contract.headline: Active undelayed core authority
contract.headline_basis: Derived from the layer rows below, not authored here, so it changes when the walk changes.

paths.name: f(x) Safe A (6 of 9)

reaction_window.basis: CallScheduled is emitted at least getMinDelay() = 259200 seconds before execution; cancel power sits with the same Safe that proposes

paths.hand_walk: The proxy's EIP-1967 implementation slot holds 0xf729422d68c2cf00574fb5712972454cf402a9b1 (verified FxUSDRegeneracy) and its admin slot holds ProxyAdmin 0x9b54b7703551d9d0ced177a78367560a8b2edda4, whose owner() is TimelockController 0x68863fb8855b04509a835082478d6e3d0be4e61a with getMinDelay() = 259200. Live hasRole over five subjects reproduced the Safe as sole PROPOSER and CANCELLER, the Safe plus address zero as EXECUTOR, the timelock as sole TIMELOCK_ADMIN, and nobody as DEFAULT_ADMIN; getRoleAdmin of every role is TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE, so no grant path exists outside a scheduled operation. Seven RoleGranted and two RoleRevoked events from deployment on 2026-04-06 reconstruct the same table; the deployer EOA and the Safe lost TIMELOCK_ADMIN on 2026-04-20. Pair simulation: ProxyAdmin.upgrade(fxUSD, dEaD) from the timelock reaches "new implementation is not a contract", and from the Safe or dEaD reverts "Ownable: caller is not the owner". MIN_DELAY() and MINIMUM_DELAY() revert, so there is no constant floor; updateDelay(0) succeeds only with the timelock as sender and reverts "caller must be timelock" from the Safe and from dEaD, so a reduction is itself delayed 72h, which is the floor recorded. The Safe has no modules and a zero guard slot. The timelock has scheduled nine operations and executed seven; the two never executed are acceptOwnership() on the two collateral price oracles.

layers.target_name: fxUSD mint, burn and legacy unwrap
layers.terminal_name: PoolManager (code-bound) and Diamond router (Safe A owned)

paths.name: f(x) PoolManager
paths.via: onlyPoolManager on mint(address,uint256) and burn(address,uint256); immutable pointer

reaction_window.basis: mint and burn execute inside user position operations with no scheduling

paths.reach_bound: No discretionary mint function exists on the minter: fxUSD is minted only inside operate/borrow accounting against registered pool collateral, capped per pool by debtCapacity (150,000,000 for the wstETH pool and 200,000,000 for the WBTC pool), and burned on repay, redeem, rebalance, liquidate and reduceDebt.
paths.hand_walk: FxUSDRegeneracy stores poolManager as an immutable and gates mint and burn with onlyPoolManager; live poolManager() on the token is 0x250893ca4ba5d05626c785e8da758026928fcd24 and that proxy's admin slot is the same ProxyAdmin as the token's, so the mint authority is code-bound today and changeable only through the 72h upgrade path. getPoolInfo returned debt capacities of 150,000,000 and 200,000,000 fxUSD against 8,786,911 and 76,591,690 fxUSD of live debt. totalSupply was 85,378,865 fxUSD.

paths.name: f(x) Diamond router (owner: Safe A)
paths.via: MIGRATOR_ROLE -> unwrap(baseToken, amount, receiver) on legacy v1 markets

reaction_window.basis: the Diamond's owner can change facets and call unwrap without scheduling

paths.reach_bound: unwrap burns the caller's own fxUSD and releases legacy fToken; it is bounded by the caller's balance and by the 264 fxUSD of legacy supply.
paths.hand_walk: MIGRATOR_ROLE was granted once, on 2025-01-02, to the Diamond and never revoked; live hasRole confirmed it and dEaD did not hold it. The Diamond's owner() is Safe A. DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE on fxUSD, which can grant MIGRATOR_ROLE, moved from Safe A to the timelock on 2026-04-20 and live hasRole shows the timelock holding it and Safe A not. getMarkets() returned two legacy v1 markets (wstETH and sfrxETH fTokens) with mintCap set to the maximum uint256, so permissionless wrap of v1 fTokens into fxUSD remains open; legacyTotalSupply() was 264 fxUSD.

layers.target_name: PoolManager global pause and per-pool borrow/redeem status
layers.terminal_name: Safe A, Safe C (3 of 4 from the same nine), deployer EOA on the WBTC pool

paths.name: f(x) deployer EOA
paths.via: EMERGENCY_ROLE on the WBTC long pool -> updateBorrowAndRedeemStatus

reaction_window.basis: a single externally owned key calls the pool directly

paths.reach_bound: WBTC long pool only; the same key holds no role on the wstETH pool or the PoolManager
paths.hand_walk: The WBTC pool's RoleGranted history shows EMERGENCY_ROLE granted to the deployer at pool deployment and never revoked; live hasRole is true on the WBTC pool and false on the wstETH pool and on the PoolManager for the same key, which is the negative control. The deployer EOA has nonce 1416 and no code.

paths.name: f(x) Safe C (3 of 4; all four owners are among Safe A's nine)
paths.via: EMERGENCY_ROLE on PoolManager and all four pools -> setPause / updateBorrowAndRedeemStatus

reaction_window.basis: a Safe transaction executes on signature collection with no on-chain scheduling

paths.hand_walk: getThreshold() = 3 and getOwners() returned four addresses, every one of which is an owner of Safe A. EMERGENCY_ROLE was granted to this Safe on the PoolManager on 2025-04-23 and on each pool at deployment; live hasRole is true on the PoolManager and the WBTC pool. setPause halts every PoolManager entry point including redeem; fxUSD transfers themselves have no pause. PoolManager paused() read false.

paths.name: f(x) Safe A (6 of 9)
paths.via: EMERGENCY_ROLE on PoolManager and all four pools

reaction_window.basis: a Safe transaction executes on signature collection with no on-chain scheduling

paths.hand_walk: The 2026-04-20 hardening added the timelock and Safe C to EMERGENCY_ROLE without revoking Safe A; live hasRole confirms Safe A on the PoolManager and both long pools. The timelock also holds the role, so the delayed route exists alongside the undelayed ones, and the layer records the undelayed worst case.

layers.target_name: pool price-oracle pointer, capacities, ratios, fees, rate provider, redemption band
layers.terminal_name: deployer EOA (WBTC pool oracle), Safe A, Safe C, 72h timelock

paths.name: f(x) deployer EOA
paths.via: EMERGENCY_ROLE on the WBTC long pool -> updatePriceOracle(address)

reaction_window.basis: a single externally owned key calls the pool directly; the setter stores any address with no validation

paths.reach_bound: WBTC long pool only (1,292 WBTC of collateral, 76,591,690 fxUSD of debt at the observed block); within that pool the price pointer decides borrow limits, rebalance and liquidation, so the bound is the pool, not the action.
paths.hand_walk: Pair simulation of updatePriceOracle(dEaD) on the WBTC pool: from the deployer EOA it succeeds, from Safe A and the timelock it succeeds, from dEaD it reverts AccessControlUnauthorizedAccount. The identical call on the wstETH pool from the deployer reverts with the deployer's own address in the error, so the key's reach is one pool. BasePool's _updatePriceOracle stores the address without an interface check.

paths.name: f(x) Safe C (3 of 4 from Safe A's nine)
paths.via: EMERGENCY_ROLE on both long pools and both short pools -> updatePriceOracle; ASSET_MANAGER_ROLE on the PoolManager and the stability pool -> manage

reaction_window.basis: a Safe transaction executes on signature collection with no on-chain scheduling

paths.hand_walk: Three of these four keys can replace the price oracle of every pool in one undelayed transaction each. Live hasRole for EMERGENCY_ROLE is true on the WBTC pool and the PoolManager; the role history shows the same grant on the wstETH pool and both short pools with no revoke.

paths.name: f(x) Safe A (6 of 9)
paths.via: EMERGENCY_ROLE on all four pools -> updatePriceOracle; ASSET_MANAGER_ROLE on the PoolManager and the stability pool -> manage

reaction_window.basis: a Safe transaction executes on signature collection with no on-chain scheduling

paths.hand_walk: Same role, same pools, at the 6-of-9 threshold. Over the last sixty executed Safe transactions every recovered signer was one of the nine owners, eight of the nine signed at least once, and quorum was met by rotating subsets rather than one fixed six.

paths.name: f(x) TimelockController (72h)
paths.via: DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE on PoolManager, both pools, PoolConfiguration and FxUSDPriceOracle

reaction_window.basis: CallScheduled precedes execution by getMinDelay() = 259200 seconds

paths.hand_walk: The delayed route covers pool capacities, debt-ratio range, rebalance and liquidation ratios, fee ratios, the wstETH rate provider, strategy allocation, pool registration, and the redemption gate's inputs: FxUSDPriceOracle.updateMaxPriceDeviation (live band 0.002 either side of one dollar) and updateCurvePool. PoolConfiguration's EMERGENCY_ROLE, which could repoint that oracle without delay, has never been granted to anyone. Four executed timelock operations so far were capacity and debt-ratio updates.

layers.target_name: StETHPriceOracle and WBTCPriceOracle (collateral prices), FxUSDPriceOracle (peg gate)
layers.terminal_name: Safe A as un-transferred owner; timelock on the peg oracle

paths.name: f(x) Safe A (6 of 9)
paths.via: Ownable2Step owner on both collateral price oracles

reaction_window.basis: onlyOwner setters execute in the Safe transaction that calls them

paths.hand_walk: owner() on 0x0c5c61025f047cb7e3e85852dc8eafd7b9a4abfb and 0xb3c90e64eb6f456a5f5c17aa99b6aeca6f4a6390 returned Safe A and pendingOwner() returned the timelock on both. acceptOwnership() for both was scheduled through the timelock on 2026-04-20 as its first operation and has no matching CallExecuted, so the handover is pending and the Safe remains the live owner. The owner sets the spot sources behind the min and max prices the pools consume and the deviation that filters them, and the deviation setter has no upper bound in code. The anchor price derives from constructor-fixed Chainlink encodings. The peg oracle behind the redemption gate is a separate proxy whose DEFAULT_ADMIN is the timelock. Both collateral oracles are non-upgradeable and were deployed 2025-03-17.

layers.target_name: pool collateral held by the PoolManager
layers.terminal_name: Safe C / Safe A move collateral into a timelock-allocated Aave strategy

paths.name: f(x) Safe C (3 of 4 from Safe A's nine)
paths.via: ASSET_MANAGER_ROLE -> manage(asset, amount) on the PoolManager

reaction_window.basis: a Safe transaction executes on signature collection with no on-chain scheduling

paths.reach_bound: manage can only transfer an asset into the strategy that DEFAULT_ADMIN (timelock) allocated for it, up to that allocation's capacity; the strategy's deposit, withdraw, kill and execute are onlyOperator where operator is the PoolManager, so the funds remain recallable by the PoolManager and cannot be sent elsewhere by the asset manager.
paths.hand_walk: allocations(wstETH) on the PoolManager returned strategy 0xfd3a6540e21d0e285f88fbfd904883b23e08f5c8 with capacity 100,000 wstETH against 5,356 wstETH held by the pool; the WBTC allocation is empty. That strategy's operator() is the PoolManager and its totalSupply() was zero, so nothing was deployed at the observed block. Safe A holds the same role; the timelock holds it too, so a delayed route exists beside the undelayed one.

unresolved: Who operates the nine Safe keys and whether any two share a person, device or vendor. Nine distinct EOAs with nine distinct first-funding sources were read; eight of nine signed at least one of the last sixty executed Safe transactions and one has never signed; that is what was measured, and independence of the keys is not asserted from it.

The Diamond router at 0x33636d49fbefbe798e15e7f356e8dbef543cc708 holds MIGRATOR_ROLE on fxUSD and OPERATOR_ROLE on the PoolManager and is owned by the 6-of-9 Safe, which can change its facets without delay. Its facet set and what OPERATOR_ROLE reaches were not walked.

Legacy v1 markets remain wrappable into fxUSD with mintCap set to the maximum value; 264 fxUSD of legacy supply exists against 85.4 million total. Administration of the v1 fToken markets and treasuries behind that path was not walked.

Chainlink aggregator governance behind the USDC/USD, ETH/USD and BTC feeds the oracles read, Curve governance over the fxUSD/USDC pool whose EMA gates redemption, and Aave governance over the strategy destination were not walked.
The short pools carry the same EMERGENCY_ROLE and TREE_COMPRESS_ROLE holders as the long pools; their internal role model beyond those roles was not enumerated.

Both collateral price oracles carry the pre-fix formula for the OpenZeppelin medium finding on minimum price deviation, because they were deployed before the audit opened and are not upgradeable; whether a corrected oracle is planned was not established. The deployed PoolManager, pools, stability pool and PoolConfiguration are a later code generation than the audited commit, and no public audit naming that Ethereum rework was located.
walk_notes: Hand-walked 2026-09-22 with read-only Ethereum calls at block 26,031,531,
plus the full role-event history and the verified sources of every contract
on the path. No transaction was signed or sent.
fxUSD and fxSAVE are ONE authority surface emitted twice. They share the
ProxyAdmin, the 72-hour TimelockController, and the 6-of-9 Safe that proposes
and cancels on it; every key that appears in this file appears in fxSAVE's.
Two rows side by side are the same people, not two controls.
Result: contract upgrades and every DEFAULT_ADMIN power sit behind a 72-hour
timelock whose only proposer and canceller is the 6-of-9 Safe. Beside that
delayed path there are UNDELAYED ones the timelock does not cover: the same
Safe and a 3-of-4 Safe drawn from the same nine keys can pause the system,
pause either collateral pool, move pool collateral into the allocated Aave
strategy, and REPLACE A POOL'S PRICE ORACLE with any address; the deployer's
single key still holds that same emergency role on the WBTC pool (76.6M fxUSD
of debt); and both collateral price oracles are still owned by the 6-of-9
Safe because the scheduled handover to the timelock was never executed.
Redemption at the PoolManager is a state gate, not a switch: it opens only
while the Curve EMA price of fxUSD is below 0.998, and borrowing closes at
the same moment. Its parameters sit behind the 72-hour timelock.
What this did NOT establish: who holds the nine keys or whether any two are
one operator; the facet set of the Diamond router that holds operator and
migrator roles; v1 legacy-market administration (264 fxUSD of legacy supply
remains wrappable with no cap); Chainlink, Curve and Aave governance behind
the price and strategy paths.
